title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married Again — and This Time, He's Doing It in His Living Room
excerpt: The perfectionist confirms his July 5 wedding to Gauri Spratt — a woman whose family story reads like one of his films
body:
The setting was as unscripted as Aamir Khan gets. Standing outside a Mumbai venue after a celebration marking 25 years of Lagaan and his production house, the actor — usually so measured with every public word — broke into a grin and told the waiting paparazzi what the whole industry had been whispering for weeks.

> "Haan, meri shaadi ho rahi hai. 5 July ko." — Aamir Khan

Just like that. No press conference. No carefully managed exclusive. The man who spent three years perfecting *Dangal's* wrestling scenes announced his third marriage like he was sharing weekend plans. And in a way, that's exactly the point. Because this wedding, by every account, is the opposite of a Bollywood production.

Aamir Khan will marry Gauri Spratt on Saturday, July 5, in a registered ceremony at his Bandra residence in Mumbai. Both families will be present. A few close friends. No reception. No guest list designed for the tabloids. "Bahut hi chhoti shaadi hai," Aamir told photographers. "Ghar pe hi kar rahe hain. Dono families hongi."

During the interaction, filmmaker Rajkumar Hirani arrived and congratulated him with a warm embrace — a moment so organic it felt like a scene the universe wrote. Aamir continued, visibly moved: "5 tareekh bahut hi khaas din hai hamare liye. Sabki duaayein chahenge hum log."

The Love Story That Took 25 Years

The most Aamir Khan thing about this love story is its timeline. He and Gauri first met nearly 25 years ago — long before she had any reason to think about Bollywood, and long before he had finished becoming one of its biggest names. They lost touch. Life happened. Marriages happened. Children happened.

Then, a few years ago, Aamir's cousin Nuzhat Khan reconnected them when Gauri visited Mumbai. What started as friendship deepened slowly, deliberately — the way Aamir approaches most things worth doing.

> ""Bahut hi chhoti shaadi hai," Aamir told photographers."

He introduced Gauri to the media before his 60th birthday celebrations in March 2025, confirming they had been together for about 18 months. She charmed reporters immediately by admitting she wasn't much of a Bollywood buff and hadn't seen many of his films. "I wanted someone who was kind, a gentleman, and just caring," she said. No mention of stardom. No mention of box office.

Who Is Gauri Spratt?

At 47, Gauri Spratt is a Bangalore-based entrepreneur — a partner and director at B Blunt, one of India's most recognisable salon chains, since 2007. She studied styling and photography at the University of the Arts London. She has a seven-year-old son, Quinn, from a previous marriage.

![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)

But the detail that makes this story feel almost cinematic is her family history. Gauri's grandfather, Philip Spratt, was a British-born Communist who came to India in the 1920s and spent the rest of his life fighting for the country's independence. He crossed an ocean and chose a cause that wasn't his by birth but became his by conviction. There's something quietly poetic about his granddaughter now making India her home in the most personal sense of the word — marrying into one of its most celebrated film families.

A Blended Family, Together

What makes the July 5 ceremony particularly touching is the involvement of children from all chapters of Aamir's life. His son Junaid and daughter Ira from his first marriage to Reena Dutta. His son Azad from his second marriage to filmmaker Kiran Rao. And Gauri's son Quinn. All of them are reportedly participating in the ceremony, with the wedding menu planned entirely by the children — a detail that says more about this family's dynamic than any official statement could.

Aamir's divorce from Kiran Rao in 2021 remains one of Bollywood's most graceful separations. They co-parent Azad, continue to collaborate professionally, and were standing on the same stage just weeks ago at the Lagaan celebration. That kind of maturity isn't common in the industry. It's barely common anywhere.

Kajol Had the Best Line

At the Lagaan 25th anniversary event, Kajol — reuniting with Aamir alongside Juhi Chawla, their co-star from *Ishq* — couldn't resist. While praising Aamir Khan Productions' track record, she remarked that his company had always shown "great taste in movies," before adding with a grin that he also had "great taste in women."

The audience roared. Aamir went visibly red. Juhi piled on. The whole evening turned into a nostalgic throwback for fans of 1990s Bollywood — three stars who defined an era, still needling each other like old friends do.

For the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who grew up on Aamir Khan's cinema — from *Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak* to *3 Idiots* to *Dangal* — this wedding feels like a chapter in a larger story they've been following for decades. Aamir's willingness to live publicly, to fail publicly, and to start again publicly has always been part of what makes him different from his contemporaries. He doesn't hide behind PR machinery. He doesn't pretend to be uncomplicated.

And this time, he's doing the most Bollywood thing in the least Bollywood way. No designer mandap. No sangeet choreographed for Instagram. Just a registered marriage in a living room, with the children cooking, and the door closed to everyone except the people who actually matter.

Saturday. July 5. Bandra.

No invitation necessary.
